transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I suppose I came in because... well, ever since the district put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, on top of my regular teaching load... which, by the way, they announced at a Friday afternoon staff meeting. Can you believe that? Our principal, Mr. Henderson, he always does things like that. He waits until 3:30 on a Friday to drop these massive administrative changes on us. Last year it was the new math curriculum, and we didn't even get the workbooks until October! The parents were just furious. I had this one mother, Mrs. Gable, calling me every single morning before the bell even rang, asking where the worksheets were, as if I print them in my basement... 

Anyway, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Right, the new rollout. I mean, I still get through the day, obviously, I've been teaching for a long time. But lately, I just feel so wound up and... discouraged. It's in a way that really isn't like me at all. I've actually started putting off my lesson plans, which I never do. And emails! I used to handle my inbox without a second thought, just knock them out during my planning period, but now I just let them sit there and pile up. I just don't feel like myself with all this extra stuff they dumped on us.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you usually do — like hobbies, activities, or even time with students or colleagues?

Well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still enjoy the kids, for the most part. Like just yesterday, little Tommy brought in this drawing of a dinosaur that he made for me. He's such a sweet boy. His mother, though... she's the one who always volunteers for the school bake sales but then brings store-bought cookies. Which, honestly, is perfectly fine, people are busy! But she takes them out of the plastic container and puts them on this fancy floral platter like she baked them herself. We all know, of course. The frosting is always that bright, unnatural blue, you know the kind? 

I actually tried making my own buttercream frosting last weekend for my nephew's birthday. He just turned seven. My sister rented one of those bouncy castles for the backyard, and let me tell you, the motor for those things is a lot louder than you'd expect. It was humming the entire afternoon, right next to the patio where the adults were trying to talk, and my brother-in-law refused to move it because he said the extension cord wouldn't reach. He's always cutting corners like that... 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. No, I still enjoy my weekends and my hobbies and all of that just fine. It's just the school paperwork that's dragging me down.
Have you found that you’re not interested in doing things that you usually enjoy, even on weekends or during your free time?

Well, like I was just saying, no, not really. I mean, my weekends are still my weekends. I actually spent this past Saturday at the garden center. They were having their end-of-season clearance, which is usually fantastic, but this year the selection was just pitiful. I was looking for some new hostas for the side yard because the ones I planted last year got completely eaten by deer. Or maybe it was rabbits? My neighbor, Mr. Abernathy, swears it's the rabbits. He put up this awful chicken wire fence around his entire property, and it looks just terrible. Like a prison yard right next to my hydrangeas! I told him he should try that spray that smells like garlic and rotten eggs, but he said he couldn't stand the smell when he sits on his porch. Which is funny, because he smokes those cheap cigars out there every evening anyway... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask? Oh, right, my free time. No, I'm still doing my usual things. I just feel so overwhelmed when I have to sit down and deal with all that new school stuff.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or having a low mood most days, even outside of work stress?

Well, no, not really. I mean, like I said, it's really just the work stuff that's got me feeling this way. Once I'm home, I'm generally fine. Except for Tuesday, when the garbage truck missed our street again. I swear, ever since the city switched to that new waste management contractor, it's been a disaster. They gave us those huge new bins with the wheels, which are supposedly easier to move, but they're so heavy when they're full! And they insist you have to face the arrows exactly toward the street, or the mechanical arm won't pick them up. Well, Mrs. Gable—you remember I mentioned her?—she lives a few blocks over, and she told me she got a warning sticker on her bin because it was angled slightly toward her driveway. A warning sticker! For garbage! I mean, who has the time to go around policing how people align their trash cans? 

Anyway, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. What were you asking about? Oh, my mood outside of work. No, I wouldn't say I'm feeling down most days. It's just that new rollout hanging over my head.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety without being able to relax?

No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't felt slow or... fidgety. I mean, I sit at my desk a lot, especially now with all this new software we're supposed to be using. They gave us these new ergonomic chairs at the beginning of the semester, which was supposed to be this big perk, but honestly, the lumbar support hits me right in the wrong spot. It's like having a tennis ball pressing into your spine all day. I tried adjusting the little knob on the side, but it's completely stuck. I asked the custodian, Jerry, if he could take a look at it, but he's been so busy ever since the pipe burst in the second-floor boys' bathroom. What a mess that was! The water came right through the ceiling tiles into the library. They had to throw out three entire shelves of biographies. It's a shame, really, some of those books were practically brand new. 

But, um, what was the question? Moving slowly? No, no, I'm moving around just fine. Just... sitting in that awful chair too much trying to figure out these new lesson plan formats.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

No, I haven't really felt unusually tired. I mean, I have my normal amount of energy. Well, except for Thursday afternoons, but that's just because they scheduled my planning period for first thing in the morning this year. By the time the final bell rings, I'm ready to head out. But speaking of heading out, the traffic right outside the school has been an absolute nightmare lately. They decided to repave Elm Street right in the middle of the school year! Can you believe it? The construction crew just leaves those orange cones everywhere, and the parents doing pickup are completely ignoring the temporary lanes. I saw one mother in a white SUV—she’s the one who always brings those store-bought cookies to bake sales and tries to pass them off as homemade, you know the type—she completely cut off a school bus! The poor bus driver was honking, and she just waved like it was nothing. It took me forty-five minutes just to get out of the parking lot on Friday. 

Oh, gosh, I'm sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask me about? Energy? Right, no, I'm not unusually tired or anything. Just exhausted by that new curriculum rollout when I sit down to do it.
Have you been feeling like you're not good at your job anymore, or that you're failing your students, even when you're doing your best?

No, I wouldn't say I feel like I'm failing them. I mean, I know I'm a good teacher. I've been doing this for over twenty years. But it's just... well, they did change the lunch schedule this year, and that's been a whole ordeal. They decided the fifth graders should eat at 11:15, which is just way too early! By the time they get back to my classroom for afternoon math, half of them are practically starving again by 1:30. And the noise in the cafeteria! I had lunch duty on Wednesday, and they replaced those nice, sturdy wooden tables with these cheap, folding plastic ones that echo every time someone drops a tray. The sound just bounces off the cinderblock walls. I asked the principal if we could put down some area rugs or something to absorb the noise, but he just gave me that look—you know, the one where he smiles but you can tell he's already thinking about his next meeting. He’s always rushing off somewhere. 

But, oh, I'm sorry. I lost my train of thought. Failing my students? No, no, I don't feel like that. I know I'm doing my best for them. It's really just the new curriculum that has me feeling overwhelmed.
Have you been having trouble concentrating on your work tasks, such as planning lessons or grading papers, more than usual lately?

Well, I am still teaching and getting through the day, but... yes, I suppose I have been having some trouble concentrating on the planning part. I've actually missed a couple of deadlines for submitting my lesson plans, which is just not like me at all. I used to be the one who had them done a week in advance! And the other day, Sarah—she teaches fourth grade down the hall from me—she had to remind me about the grade-level meeting we had scheduled. Speaking of Sarah, she just got this new golden retriever puppy, and she brings pictures to the lounge every single day. It's very cute, don't get me wrong, but she spends half of our lunch break talking about potty training. And honestly, the staff lounge is already so crowded since they moved the copy machine in there. It takes up a quarter of the room, and it's always jamming! It flashes this little red light and beeps until someone comes to fix it, which usually takes hours. I don't know why they couldn't just leave it in the main office where it belongs. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, concentrating. Yes, I've had to push back some grading, too, and my colleagues have had to remind me about a few things I normally handle without any issue. It's just hard to focus with all these new requirements.

latest_inference.note: This turn confirmed significant difficulty with concentration related to work stress, which aligns with the persistence and functional impairment criteria for F43.22. The patient continues to rule out core symptoms of depression (e.g., anhedonia, low mood, fatigue, self-blame), making F43.0 and F43.8 less likely.
